newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD says Bonn knows it can't meet EMU goal.
newsitem.headline: German SPD says Bonn knows it can't meet EMU goal.

text.p: Oskar Lafontaine, head of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), said on Monday Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government knows it cannot meet the Maastricht deficit rule with its current policies.
This view is shared by most economic research institutes and is obvious from government budget developments, Lafontaine said.

Countries hoping to participate in the single European currency aim to reduce their government deficits to three percent of gross domestic product, but many economists say Germany is unlikely to reach that target this year.
German SPD says Bonn knows it can't meet EMU goal
Lafontaine said the three-percent rule was not decisive for the SPD, since Germany could demonstrate a high degree of stability on the inflation, interest rate, and currency value guidelines.
He called for a stronger emphasis on jobs-creation policies at the European level.

Gerhard Schroeder, SPD economic spokesman and state premier of Lower Saxony, said in an interview with the Financial Times published on Monday that Germany won't meet the EMU criteria without creative accounting and called for a delay.
